question: The Commission’s reply does not answer any of the questions posed. Instead, it merely provides information on the content of the European Media Freedom Act, with which the signatories are already familiar, and states that the Commission is aware of the action plan drawn up by Pedro Sánchez’s Government.

The plan’s Axis 2 includes a measure to adopt a national strategy to counter disinformation campaigns and the establishment of a committee on disinformation in the Congress of Deputies. In view of the lack of answer: 1.
Has the Commission assessed whether the measures proposed to combat disinformation are in line with the regulation?
What steps does the Commission intend to take in the event that the measures in the action plan are used to restrict freedom of the press and control the media?

Does the Commission believe that statements made by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez branding the media outlets reporting on corruption cases against his wife, brother, political party and members of his Government as ‘far right’ pose a risk to freedom of the press?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the author: Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE)
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.2.2025) The measure referred to by the Honourable Member has been announced as part of the Spanish action plan but has not been adopted yet and, therefore, the Commission is not in a position to assess it. Also, the Commission would not assess individual political statements.

Member States have a primary responsibility to monitor the application of the European Media Freedom Act1 and to take the necessary steps for enforcement. In its role as guardian of the Treaties, the Commission will continue monitoring the situation on the independence of media and journalists and may decide to take appropriate action including, where appropriate, infringement proceedings.
It will continue assessing all relevant developments related to media freedom and pluralism in all Member States, including Spain, under the annual Rule of Law Report2.
